candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

chosen_property.label: hasFatalityRate
chosen_property.definition: Indicates the medical condition associated with a fatality rate for an infectious agent.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property for fatality rate relation; minted.

candidates.label: cvdNumC19Died
candidates.comment: A mortality count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who died in the hospital, ED, or overflow location. Also called: COVID-19 deaths, C19 fatalities, pandemic deaths. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 died "10", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 died "3", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 died "25".

candidates.label: healthPlanCoinsuranceRate
candidates.comment: A coinsurance rate relation between a health plan cost-sharing specification and the numerical rate of coinsurance. Also called coinsurance percentage, rate of coinsurance, coinsurance ratio. Examples: "Health plan cost-sharing has a coinsurance rate of 0.2.", "The specification includes a coinsurance rate of 0.15.", "This plan's coinsurance rate is 0.3."

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: diseaseSpreadStatistics
candidates.comment: A disease spread statistics relation between a special announcement and a dataset, observation, URL, or web content containing statistical information about the spread of a disease. Also called "epidemic data", "infection rates", "case statistics". Examples: "Special announcement diseaseSpreadStatistics 'Dataset of daily cases'", "Public health update diseaseSpreadStatistics 'WebContent on regional spread'", "COVID-19 alert diseaseSpreadStatistics 'URL to dashboard'".

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf
candidates.comment: A risk amplification relation between a medical risk factor and the medical entity (condition, complication) whose likelihood it increases. Also called heightens risk of, raises risk of, predisposes to, contributes to risk of. Examples: Smoking increasesRiskOf lung cancer. High blood pressure increasesRiskOf heart attack. Obesity increasesRiskOf type 2 diabetes.

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

chosen_property.label: hadPassenger
chosen_property.definition: Indicates a passenger or group of passengers on a vessel.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property for ship having passengers; minted.

candidates.label: passengerSequenceNumber
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the sequence number assigned to a passenger for a flight reservation by the airline. Also called boarding sequence, passenger number, flight sequence. Examples: A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number '001'. A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number 'A12'. A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number '34B'.

candidates.label: passengerPriorityStatus
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the priority status assigned to a passenger for a flight reservation. Also called boarding priority, security status, passenger status. Examples: A flight reservation has a passenger priority status of 'FastTrack'. A flight reservation has a passenger priority status of 'Priority Boarding'. A flight reservation has a passenger priority status of 'Elite Member'.

candidates.label: seatingCapacity
candidates.comment: The maximum number of individuals that can be accommodated with seating in a vehicle, considering both physical space and legal limits. Also called passenger capacity, seat count, number of seats. Examples: `Car Model X` seatingCapacity `5`, `Bus Model Y` seatingCapacity `50`, `Airplane Model Z` seatingCapacity `200`.

candidates.label: vehicleSeatingCapacity
candidates.comment: A vehicle seating capacity relation between a vehicle and the number of passengers it can seat. Also called seating capacity, passenger capacity, number of seats. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '5'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '7 persons'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '2'".

candidates.label: payload
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the maximum permitted weight of passengers and cargo a vehicle can carry, excluding the vehicle's own weight. Also called carrying capacity, load capacity, cargo weight limit. Examples: A truck has a payload of 1000 kg. A car has a payload of 500 kg. An aircraft has a payload of 20,000 lbs. Distinct from weight, which refers to the weight of the empty vehicle itself.

candidates.label: pickupLocation
candidates.comment: A spatial attribute indicating the place where a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be collected. Also called collection point, pick-up point, embarkation point. Examples: A taxi reservation has a pickup location of 'Grand Central Station'. A rental car reservation has a pickup location of 'Airport Terminal 1'. The ride-share booking has a pickup location at 'Home Address'.

candidates.label: seatNumber
candidates.comment: The specific identifier for a reserved seat, such as a number. Also called seat ID, seat number, specific seat. Examples: `Concert Ticket Seat` seatNumber `"27"`, `Airplane Seat` seatNumber `"14A"`, `Theater Seat` seatNumber `"Row C, Seat 5"`. Distinct from `seatRow` or `seatSection`, which are broader location indicators.

candidates.label: pickupTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the date and time when a taxi will pick up a passenger or a rental car can be collected. Also called collection time, pick-up time, embarkation time. Examples: A taxi reservation has a pickup time of '2023-12-25T08:00:00'. A rental car reservation has a pickup time of '2024-01-01T10:30:00'. The ride-share booking has a pickup time of 'now'.

candidates.label: seatingType
candidates.comment: The classification or category of a seat, indicating its type or class. Also called seat class, seat category, type of seating. Examples: `Airplane Seat` seatingType `"Economy Class"`, `Theater Seat` seatingType `"Premium"`, `Train Seat` seatingType `"First Class"`.

candidates.label: ticketedSeat
candidates.comment: An association between a ticket and the specific seat it grants access to. Also called "assigned seat", "seat number", "ticket seat allocation". Examples: "The concert ticket has ticketedSeat Row A, Seat 12", "The flight ticket's ticketedSeat is 23F", "This ticket is for a specific ticketedSeat."
